output.summary: KEP-1122 adds CSI Node Plugin support on Windows nodes by introducing csi-proxy.exe, a host-side privileged proxy exposing a GRPC API over a named pipe so CSI node plugins running in containers can perform privileged storage operations. The KEP is in implementable state at stable stage; the GA work was carried out out-of-tree in kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy rather than in kubernetes/kubernetes.
output.rationale: Windows containers cannot perform privileged operations (disk scan, partitioning, formatting, staging) that CSI node plugins need, so the KEP proposes a host OS proxy. Discussion shows the remaining work to reach GA was moved out of k/k: ddebroy stated that "all the remaining changes to reach GA/stable will be out of tree in https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy". The feature was declared complete on 2021-08-09.

alternatives.option: Make the CSI node plugin changes in kubernetes/kubernetes (in-tree k/k PRs)
alternatives.why_not: Discussion says no k/k PRs were anticipated: "We do not anticipate any k/k PRs for 1.19." and later "all changes target https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy".

alternatives.option: Use a privileged container model for Windows CSI node plugins
alternatives.why_not: The sources say this is still evolving and is not the chosen path for this KEP: "As privileged container support for Windows evolves (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2037), there may be changes necessary in k/k". The KEP's Non-Goals defer broader privileged operations to a separate KEP.

alternatives.option: Extend support to CSI controller plugins from Windows nodes
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal: "Support CSI Controller Plugin operations from Windows nodes: This may be considered in the future but not an immediate priority."

evidence.quote: This KEP describes a host OS proxy to execute privileged operations on the Windows host OS on behalf of a container.
All the remaining changes to reach GA/stable will be out of tree in https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-proxy .
We do not anticipate any k/k PRs for 1.19.
The decision is to stay Beta for 1.20 to get a better idea of what changes will be necessary around privileged containers for Windows.
This issue is now complete! https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/09/csi-windows-support-with-csi-proxy-reaches-ga/ Many thanks to all those who contributed!!
